service-contractors-and-plant-engineers-.author: Lorena Xu
service-contractors-and-plant-engineers-.core: Posted in last 7 days Service Contractors & Plant Engineers - Old Cooling Tower Fill Removal How Do You Remove Old Cooling Tower Fill? We Want to Hear Your Story We talk with cooling tower owners, contractors, and maintenance teams every day. One question keeps coming up—and it’s not about specifications or materials. It’s about the job itself: How do you actually get old fill out of a cooling tower? If you’ve ever replaced cooling tower fill, you know it’s rarely as simple as pulling it out. Old fill can be wet, heavy, brittle, scaled, fouled, or stuck in places that seem impossible to reach. So we’d like to ask our customers and readers: Do you remove old fill by hand, piece by piece? Do you cut it into sections first? What tools work best? Do you use a crane, winch, rope, chute, conveyor, or vacuum system? Do you pull it from the top, side, or bottom? How do you handle wet, dirty, or contaminated fill? What safety procedures are non-negotiable? What do you do with the old fill afterward—landfill, recycling, or special disposal?What’s one tip you’d give someone doing this for the first time? We’re collecting real-world methods from service contractors, plant engineers, facility managers, and OEM technicians. Your experience could help someone else complete a safer, faster, and cleaner fill replacement.Share your answer in the comments. Photos and short videos are welcome. With your permission, we may feature your method in a future article. #TJLATINO #Cooligngtowerfillreplacement #coolingtowerupdate

residents-near-data-centers-in-western-n.headline: Residents Near Data Centers in Western NC - Noise Complaints & Records
residents-near-data-centers-in-western-n.author: Elijah Skipper
residents-near-data-centers-in-western-n.core: Posted in last 7 days Residents Near Data Centers in Western NC - Noise Complaints & Records I followed up with data center neighbors 13 years after their noise complaints. The yard is quieter, but I still had questions. Hey everyone! I'm Elijah Skipper, an investigative reporter at News 13 in western North Carolina. I wanted to introduce myself and share a follow-up I recently finished. A lot of the discussion is about proposed data centers. I was interested in what happened after one opened and neighbors started having problems. Our station reported on generator noise at Facebook's Forest City site in 2013. I tracked down two of the neighbors from that story, Jim Bennett and Tommy Doggett, and went back to see them. We started by watching their old interviews. Then we went into Jim's backyard, right beside the site, and listened. They say things are much better now. They believe the sound-absorbing material and trees helped, and they say Facebook eventually became a better neighbor. Both also believe the original reporting helped get the company to listen. It took time, though. Residents were still complaining in our 2015 follow-up. I looked through the previous coverage and records and followed up with Meta about what changed and whether those changes influenced its policies at other sites. At publication, we hadn't obtained a current testing schedule or written agreement showing what hours apply now. I'd like to hear from people who have been through the complaint process. What could residents get enforced, and what depended on the company voluntarily following through? If you've found records that helped answer those questions locally, I'd be interested in hearing about them. WLOS

Detectives were investigating the incident. I’m hoping to hear from Hyattsville residents and local business owners about their perspectives on commercial break-ins and public safety in the community. Have you experienced or witnessed a similar incident? Have you noticed any changes in safety around local businesses, or do you have thoughts on how these incidents affect the community? I’m interested in hearing different perspectives and am not assuming this incident is part of a larger trend. I would appreciate the opportunity to speak with anyone willing to share their experiences or thoughts for my story. If you’re interested, please comment below or send me a DM. former-diplomats-and-trade-negotiators-i.core: Posted in last 7 days Former Diplomats & Trade Negotiators - India-US Trade Negotiations Looking for Experts | India–US Trade Negotiations India and the United States are negotiating a bilateral trade agreement at a time when tariffs, market access and broader strategic considerations are increasingly intertwined. But the negotiations raise questions that extend beyond trade figures and tariff concessions. What are the principal sticking points? How much negotiating room does New Delhi have? Can India and the US compartmentalise their trade disagreements without affecting the broader strategic partnership? And what would a mutually beneficial agreement actually look like? I am working on an article for The India Interest examining these questions and their implications for India's economic and foreign-policy interests. I am looking to incorporate perspectives from former diplomats, trade negotiators, economists, international trade specialists and researchers working on India–US relations. The format is straightforward: two or three brief questions, with responses incorporated into the article and duly attributed. No recorded interview is required. I would particularly welcome perspectives that go beyond the immediate negotiations and examine their longer-term implications for India–US relations. If you work in any of these areas, or know someone whose insights could contribute to this discussion, I would be glad to connect. #IndiaUSRelations #TradeNegotiations #IndiaUS #ForeignPolicy #InternationalTrade #Geopolitics #TheIndiaInterest

cios-and-ai-leaders-ai-infrastructure-da.core: Posted in last 7 days CIOs & AI Leaders - AI Infrastructure Day-2 Ops & Costs I am working on a CIO&Leader (ET Edge) cover story themed around "𝗜𝗻𝗳𝗿𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗔𝗜". Most AI infrastructure talk stops at the build or the buy. We're interested in what happens after the pilot: running AI in production, on a budget, under regulation, with someone accountable when it fails. 𝗧𝗵𝗿𝗲𝗲 𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗮𝘀 𝘄𝗲 𝘄𝗮𝗻𝘁 𝘁𝗼 𝗲𝘅𝗽𝗹𝗼𝗿𝗲: 1. Where AI runs, and how readiness is judged before a pilot gets capacity 2. What you can see once it's live, and what it really costs 3. Who owns it on day two: model retirements, agent identity, compliance clocks We're looking for end-user businesses from: • 𝗥𝗲𝗴𝘂𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗕𝗙𝗦𝗜 • 𝗠𝗮𝗻𝘂𝗳𝗮𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗶𝗻𝗱𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗮𝗹 • 𝗜𝗧 𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘃𝗶𝗰𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗚𝗖𝗖𝘀 • 𝗣𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗺𝗮 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗵𝗲𝗮𝗹𝘁𝗵𝗰𝗮𝗿𝗲 • 𝗥𝗲𝘁𝗮𝗶𝗹 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘀𝘂𝗺𝗲𝗿 • 𝗔𝗣𝗜-𝗳𝗶𝗿𝘀𝘁 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗰𝗹𝗼𝘂𝗱-𝗼𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗽𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗲𝘀 • 𝗠𝗶𝗱-𝗺𝗮𝗿𝗸𝗲𝘁 CIOs, CTOs, CISOs, CFOs and AI leaders, we'd like to hear from you, especially on what stalled and what you reversed. healthtech-ceos-and-founders-turning-dem.headline: HealthTech CEOs & Founders - Turning Demos Into Real-World Use
healthtech-ceos-and-founders-turning-dem.author: Segun Aboderin MBA, MEIE
healthtech-ceos-and-founders-turning-dem.core: Posted in last 7 days HealthTech CEOs & Founders - Turning Demos Into Real-World Use What does it take to turn a healthcare problem into a solution people can use? A healthcare solution can work brilliantly in a demo. What does it take to make it work in someone’s life? That’s the question myself and Tomisin Adelowo are exploring at Toronto Metropolitan University From safer patient transfers and better pharmacy services to chronic pain support, faster clinical communication and earlier disease detection, we’re curious about the journey behind the innovation. What did patients teach you that changed your idea? Who did you have to convince? What nearly stopped you? If you’re a CEO or founder building a healthcare, medical or wellness business, IoT etc we’d love to hear your story. As part of our program in Engineering Innovation and Entrepreneurship, we’re looking to interview an entrepreneur and spend a day shadowing their team to understand the decisions, setbacks and breakthroughs behind their solution. Open to sharing your journey? Send me a message. Know someone we should meet? Tag them or introduce us. #HealthTech #HealthcareInnovation #Entrepreneurship #TMU Picture credit: Alta Platform, Able Innovations
